security.justification: Every trust boundary is open. The local server binds 0.0.0.0 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every response; the agent fetched the user's real league data from the LAN and confirmed cross-origin POST to /sync is accepted. That file is polled every 3s and rendered through ~40 unescaped innerHTML template literals — a working PoC pushed a hostile payload through the real mapper and renderers and got 9 confirmed injections across 5 panels. Path traversal is correctly blocked, there are no dependencies, and no secrets appear in git history.

findings.title: Server binds all interfaces, not localhost
findings.evidence: server_address = ('', PORT). lsof shows TCP *:8000. Fetched /imported_league.json from the LAN IP: 200, 26287 bytes of private league data.
findings.fix: server_address = ('127.0.0.1', PORT).

findings.title: Wildcard CORS turns the server into a read/write API for any website
findings.evidence: end_headers unconditionally sends ACAO: * on all responses; do_OPTIONS answers every preflight 200. do_POST never checks Origin, Referer or Content-Type. Any page the user visits can read every served file and overwrite imported_league.json.
findings.fix: Echo ACAO only for the extension origin and http://localhost:8000; reject do_POST unless Origin matches; require a shared secret header.

findings.title: Scraped DOM text and third-party JSON interpolated into innerHTML with no escaping
findings.evidence: grep for escapeHtml/sanitiz/DOMPurify across js/ returns nothing. PoC through the real importScrapedPayload + renderers confirmed 9 unescaped injections in #home-recommendations, #draft-recent-picks, #draft-rec-panel, #league-team-profile-container, #settings-league-name.
findings.fix: Add one esc() helper and wrap every non-numeric interpolation; prefer textContent for name cells. Add a CSP meta to index.html.

findings.title: Player id interpolated into a JS string inside an onclick attribute
findings.evidence: onclick="window.store.recordDraftPick(${currentPick}, '${p.id}')". p.id for unresolved players is MOCK_${playerName.replace(/\s+/g,'_')} — only whitespace touched. PoC confirmed X'); alert(document.domain); // survives into rendered HTML.
findings.fix: Remove the inline handlers (a real listener is already bound 80 lines below) and sanitise the id via playerKey.

findings.title: Trade DM text injected into an onclick with only single quotes escaped
findings.evidence: onclick="navigator.clipboard.writeText('${p.dmText.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}')". dmText embeds scraped manager and player names; the browser parses HTML before JS, so a double quote ends the attribute.
findings.fix: Delete the inline handler; attach btn.onclick alongside the existing trade-btn binding.

findings.title: postMessage bridge accepts forged messages from any script in the page
findings.evidence: Only check is event.source !== window — trivially satisfied by any script in the frame. No origin check. manifest all_frames: true, so it is live in every ESPN subframe. Any ad or third-party tag can post a GRIDIRON_EDGE_SYNC payload that the extension POSTs to localhost.
findings.fix: Check event.origin === 'https://fantasy.espn.com' and replace the ambient channel with a MessageChannel port; validate payload shape.

findings.title: Service worker forwards arbitrary payloads with no sender or schema validation
findings.evidence: onMessage listener never inspects sender.origin/url/tab; message.data goes straight to disk with no size, depth or key constraints.
findings.fix: Gate on sender.url startsWith https://fantasy.espn.com/ and schema-check message.data before forwarding.

findings.title: Serves the entire working directory including .git, with directory listings
findings.evidence: Falls through to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler. curl /.git/config returned 200 with the real repo config; /test/ returned a 943-byte auto index.
findings.fix: Override translate_path to an explicit allowlist and list_directory to return 403.

findings.title: Unbounded request body read
findings.evidence: content_length read with no cap, on a ThreadingHTTPServer reachable cross-origin. A visited page can send a multi-gigabyte body.
findings.fix: Reject > 5MB before reading; read in bounded chunks.

findings.title: Raw exception text reflected to the client
findings.evidence: json.dumps({'status':'error','message':str(e)}) returns filesystem paths and internal detail to a cross-origin caller.
findings.fix: Return a fixed string; log detail server-side only.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy
findings.evidence: No CSP meta tag and server.py sends no CSP header. Nothing constrains inline handlers, javascript: URLs, or exfiltration once XSS lands.
findings.fix: Add a CSP meta limiting script-src to 'self' and connect-src to the three known API hosts (requires removing inline onclick first).

findings.title: Extension permissions broader than the task needs
findings.evidence: permissions includes tabs (URL and title of every tab) where activeTab suffices; all_frames: true on both content scripts widens the postMessage forgery surface.
findings.fix: Drop tabs; set all_frames: false; reconsider clipboardWrite.

findings.title: Page-controlled error text written to the popup's innerHTML
findings.evidence: statusEl.innerHTML with errorText joined from res.result.error, which originates in the MAIN world of the ESPN page. MV3 CSP makes this markup injection rather than script execution today.
findings.fix: Use textContent throughout; build the coloured span with createElement.

findings.title: Entire persisted state restored from localStorage with no validation
findings.evidence: this.state = JSON.parse(data) wholesale replaces defaultState, so missing keys are not backfilled and attacker-chosen keys survive.
findings.fix: Merge over defaults and validate the shape of leagues/playerDatabase.

findings.title: Quota exhaustion silently discards writes
findings.evidence: save() catches everything and only console.errors. recordWeeklyMetrics appends up to 40 entries per player across 523 players. Past ~5MB every pick is silently lost.
findings.fix: Detect QuotaExceededError specifically, surface it, and prune before retrying.

findings.title: Launcher unconditionally kills whatever holds port 8000
findings.evidence: lsof -ti:$PORT | xargs kill with no check on what the PID actually is.
findings.fix: Confirm the PID's command line before killing.

findings.title: Full league payload written to the clipboard on server failure
findings.evidence: navigator.clipboard.writeText(JSON.stringify(data)) in the catch — the complete authenticated ESPN response sits in the clipboard readable by any focused app.
findings.fix: Prompt first, or offer a download instead.

findings.title: Unvalidated league id interpolated into a URL
findings.evidence: Template-literal interpolation with no format check and no encodeURIComponent; a value containing ? # or / alters the request path.
findings.fix: Require /^\d+$/ and encodeURIComponent.

findings.title: 14.6MB Sleeper player dictionary downloaded on every trending refresh
findings.evidence: getJSON(SLEEPER_PLAYERS) inside fetchTrending's Promise.all, no size ceiling, no schema check before lookups.
findings.fix: Cache for the session; sanity-check Content-Length before parsing.

security.verified: Read server.py, the full extension, store.js, player-database.js, news-monitor.js and ~1500 lines of app.js/espn-client.js. Triaged 112 innerHTML-class sites. Ran a working XSS PoC through the real modules. Probed the live server: LAN binding, ACAO:*, .git/config served, directory listings, cross-origin POST preflight approved. Confirmed path traversal blocked on three encodings. git log --all -S for 12 secret patterns: nothing. Confirmed no dependency manifest exists. Ran all 9 test files: 260 assertions, 0 failures.
security.notChecked: Did not POST to /sync (would overwrite the user's real league file). Did not load the extension in a real Chrome profile, so postMessage forgery and popup injection are established by reading. Did not execute the XSS in a real browser DOM — the stub proves the data reaches the sink, not that script runs. No authenticated ESPN session, so the real-API branch of mapESPNLeague was read but not exercised.

tests.justification: The suite is real and non-trivial — 9 files, 260 executed checks, passing in ~1.4s with no network and no clock dependence — and the four statistically validated engines are genuinely well covered (auction-advisor 97%, roster-manager 98%, team-strength and bracket-strategy 100%). But measured coverage is 55.60% overall and the gap falls entirely on the layer between browser and engines: espn-client 13.62%, store.js 31.77%, renderDraftPage 0%. Two of this week's shipped-bug classes would recur undetected today.

findings.title: The live-draft page is excluded from the render smoke test, and it throws
findings.evidence: PAGES lists nine renderers; renderDraftPage is not among them. Substituting it gives 0 passed / 3 failed: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0') at js/app.js:1135 — league.draftState.draftOrder[teamIndex]. Lines 1106-1548 are 0% covered.
findings.fix: Add renderDraftPage to PAGES and draftOrder/currentNominationBid/currentNominationMax to buildLeague(); harden app.js:1135 with (league.draftState.draftOrder || []).

findings.title: The entire scrape-resolve-attribute pipeline has zero test coverage
findings.evidence: Coverage: espn-client.js 13.62% line. Lines 60-116 (importScrapedPayload) and 210-390 (the DOM transform that resolves names, mints MOCK_ players and attributes picks) are entirely unexecuted. No test file imports espn-client.js. The ownerId === null guard has never been run.
findings.fix: Add test/espn-client.test.mjs driving importScrapedPayload with the real imported_league.json plus mutated variants (unknown name, null drafterTeamId, missing position, duplicate pick, empty picks, null payload).

findings.title: The popup ships a stale duplicate scraper carrying every already-fixed bug, untested
findings.evidence: manifest sets popup.html as the browser action and popup.html:120 has a live sync-btn, so this is a real user path. popup.js:397 seenPicks = new Set() and :421 dedupe-by-pick-number is the exact pre-fix logic; :430 reinstates the position+team requirement that drops every D/ST. No bidAmount capture, no DST aliases, no rejection log. test/scraper.test.mjs loads only content-main.js.

findings.title: 0% function coverage on the snake-draft recommendation engine
findings.evidence: Coverage: 2.72% line, 0% function. Both exports unexecuted; their only call sites are inside renderDraftPage, which no test calls. Line 52-53 has the same unguarded draftOrder dereference that crashes app.js:1135.
findings.fix: Add test/draft-assistant.test.mjs over mockLeague asserting primaryPick is undrafted, alternatives >= 4, flex counted once, and graceful degradation with no draftOrder.

findings.title: 0% function coverage on the Monte Carlo season simulator
findings.evidence: Coverage: 1.80% line, 0% function. render.test.mjs hard-codes schedule: [], so all three scenarios take the preseasonOutlook branch and runSeasonSimulation is never called. 388 lines including an unseeded Math.random weather roll have never executed.
findings.fix: Add a fourth render scenario with a populated schedule, plus test/simulator.test.mjs with an injectable rng.

findings.title: A valid-but-partial stored state silently produces undefined collections, then a TypeError
findings.evidence: this.state = JSON.parse(data) with no merge against defaultState. Probe seeding {currentLeagueId, activeTab} (valid JSON, so the catch never fires) gave state.leagues undefined, then getActiveLeague() threw TypeError.
findings.fix: this.state = { ...defaultState, ...JSON.parse(data) } and add test/store.test.mjs covering absent key, corrupt JSON, partial schema, null leagues.

findings.title: localStorage quota failure is swallowed and never reaches the UI or listeners
findings.evidence: notify() sits inside the try, so on failure no listener fires. Probe with a throwing setItem printed 'listeners notified after quota failure: 0'. The app keeps rendering state that was never persisted.
findings.fix: Set a persistFailed flag, still notify, and surface a banner using the existing banner machinery. Test with an injected QuotaExceededError.

findings.title: No package.json, no CI, no test script, no single documented command
findings.evidence: No package.json, no .github/, no Makefile, no lockfiles. node --test test/*.test.mjs works but is documented nowhere. BACKTEST.md names 2 of 9 files with stale counts (says 27 and 44; actual 42 and 51).
findings.fix: Add package.json with type:module and test/coverage scripts, plus a GitHub Actions workflow. Update BACKTEST.md.

findings.title: The parse guard covers js/ only, leaving every shipped extension file unchecked
findings.evidence: walk(join(ROOT, 'js')) — 14 files. Not walked: all 7 chrome-extension/*.js including the 809-line content-main.js and 687-line popup.js, the files most often edited during a draft.
findings.fix: Walk ['js','chrome-extension'] plus bookmarklet.js; check extension files as classic scripts in a second pass.

findings.title: Five checks sit behind unguarded ifs and vanish silently if the fixture shifts
findings.evidence: if (filled.length === 5), if (spare && hole), if (hole2) — none has an else branch asserting the precondition. Nothing asserts an expected total, so lost checks are undetectable. These include the two headline Part 16 regressions.
findings.fix: Add else check(..., false) to each guard and assert a floor on the total count.

findings.title: The render fixture is not shaped like real espn-client output
findings.evidence: buildLeague() omits draftOrder (espn-client always sets it), sets schedule: [] (suppressing the simulator), omits currentNominationBid/Max. The DOM stub returns querySelectorAll: () => [] unconditionally, so any renderer loop over queried nodes is a no-op.
findings.fix: Build the fixture by calling importScrapedPayload on the real imported_league.json — one fixture tests pipeline and renderers together.

findings.title: The dedup replace-the-poorer-row branch is never exercised
findings.evidence: Instrumenting the scraper with the shipped ROWS shows only the score <= prior.score path runs. Reordering so panel rows come first produced 'replaced a poorer row' and still resolved correctly. ESPN does not guarantee ordering.
findings.fix: Add a second scrapeDraftDOM pass over reversed ROWS asserting the same 6 picks and drafters.

findings.title: A global unhandledRejection no-op swallows every async failure
findings.evidence: process.on('unhandledRejection', () => {}) is process-wide, not scoped to the intended feed noise. A genuine bug in checkDraftReadiness or refreshNewsAndRerender is discarded and the file still exits 0.
findings.fix: Record rejections and assert only the expected ones match /network disabled in tests/.

findings.title: The news feed functions are untested despite the header claiming a dead feed is handled
findings.evidence: No test calls fetchLeagueNews, fetchTrending or refreshNews. Uncovered: relevanceTo, the getJSON error branch, the whole article-parsing loop, refreshNews's tail. fetchLeagueNews has no try/catch of its own.
findings.fix: Stub fetch for 500 / empty-articles / malformed JSON and assert refreshNews returns empty-but-valid rather than throwing.

findings.title: A dead second test runner that cannot load and has tested nothing since the initial commit
findings.evidence: Imports ./js/engine/waiver-evaluator.js, which does not exist (replaced by roster-manager.js). The module 404s so every assertion is dead. Its assertions were weak anyway — one asserts a literal in the fixture it imports.
findings.fix: Delete test.html or repoint it and wire it into the suite.

findings.title: Only 2 of ~15 scraper functions are reachable from the test
findings.evidence: scraper.test.mjs returns only { scrapeDraftDOM, findDraftSummaryContainer }. Untested: findCurrentNomination (feeds the live bid), scrapeTeamsAndBudgets (feeds every rival's purchasing power), findMyTeamNameFromDOM (decides myTeamId), checkAndSync.
findings.fix: Expose these from the extraction and add DOM fixtures, especially for budgets and myTeamId.

findings.title: Only well-formed rows; no malformed-payload cases
findings.evidence: All 9 fixture rows are clean. Nothing exercises an empty container, undefined innerText, UI chrome, oversized rows, a $99999 bid, or a forced throw. The 'it did not throw' check reads a global that is never set in the happy path, so it passes without proving the error channel works.
findings.fix: Add a malformed-input block asserting null return, a populated scrape-error global on a forced throw, and a recorded reason for every dropped row.

findings.title: The sync endpoint has zero tests and overwrites a good league file with any valid JSON
findings.evidence: do_POST json.loads then immediately dumps to imported_league.json with no schema check and no size limit — POSTing null or {} replaces a live draft's data. /health is likewise untested. No Python test exists anywhere.
findings.fix: Add test/test_server.py against a ThreadingHTTPServer on port 0; validate a minimum shape before writing and write atomically via temp file + rename.

findings.title: preseasonOutlook takes an rng parameter no test supplies
findings.evidence: Signature is (league, runs = 2000, rng = Math.random); all four call sites omit the third argument while asserting strict inequalities across Monte Carlo runs. 25 consecutive runs gave 0 failures, so the flakiness is latent, not absent.
findings.fix: Pass a seeded PRNG in every call; it makes failures reproducible and lets runs drop.

findings.title: Render checks assert only 'did not throw'
findings.evidence: 27 of 33 checks are check(`${name} renders`, !err). Only two per scenario assert content. A page that renders structurally valid but numerically wrong output passes.
findings.fix: Assert one load-bearing element per page received plausible content.

findings.title: Smoke-only coverage on lineup-optimizer and trade-generator, plus a duplicated lineup solver
findings.evidence: Coverage 67% and 52%, both reached only incidentally via renderers. No test asserts optimizeLineup returns a legal lineup. team-strength.js bestLineup is a second independent solver and IS directly tested; the two can silently disagree.
findings.fix: Add test/lineup-optimizer.test.mjs reusing the team-strength assertions plus a cross-check that both solvers agree on the same roster.

findings.title: elCache persists across scenarios while written is cleared
findings.evidence: written.clear() runs per scenario but elCache is module-scope and never reset, so innerText/value set in scenario 1 leak into 2 and 3.
findings.fix: elCache.clear() inside load().

findings.title: process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0) forces a zero exit
findings.evidence: An explicit exit(0) overrides any nonzero code node would otherwise set. Four files do this; the other five use the safer if (failed) process.exit(1).
findings.fix: Use if (failed) process.exit(1) everywhere.

tests.verified: Ran node --test test/*.test.mjs: 9 files, 260 checks, 0 failures, ~1.4s. Ran each file individually and recorded per-file counts. Verified failure propagation by flipping an assertion in a scratch copy — exits 1. Ran --experimental-test-coverage for real per-file numbers (55.60% line overall). Reproduced the renderDraftPage TypeError under the project's own fixture in all three scenarios. Reproduced the store.js partial-state TypeError and the silent quota path. Instrumented the real scraper in both DOM orderings. Confirmed no package.json, no CI, and that waiver-evaluator.js does not exist.
tests.notChecked: No browser-real behaviour — every render test runs against a DOM stub whose querySelectorAll always returns []. The extension against a live ESPN draft room. V8 coverage does not instrument chrome-extension/*.js (loaded via new Function), so scraper reachability comes from reading the extraction. Numerical correctness of the engines themselves — assessed whether tests exist and are meaningful, not whether the maths is right.

documentation.justification: The in-code documentation in the rewritten engines and the test suite is exceptional — all ten test files explain the specific failure they guard against, and several modules run 23-35% comment density with real 'why' reasoning. But the repo has no README at all, the Reproducing section is non-reproducible (the harness lives in an ephemeral /private/tmp scratchpad and both cited test counts are wrong), and at least eight documented statements are now factually false — including a paragraph contradicting three other parts of the same document, and a shipped UI panel of fabricated player news that is never replaced at runtime.

findings.title: No README exists; nothing tells a newcomer how to run the app
findings.evidence: 44 tracked files, no README, no package.json, no CLAUDE.md. The only run prose is chrome-extension/README.md, which says python3 server.py but never says to open http://localhost:8000. The app cannot run from file:// (two fetches of same-origin paths), so the server is mandatory and documented nowhere. Start Gridiron Edge.command is the real entry point and is mentioned in no document.
findings.fix: Add a root README covering prerequisites, both start paths, that projections ship in-repo, how league data arrives, and the test command.

findings.title: The Reproducing section cannot reproduce anything, and both its numbers are wrong
findings.evidence: Says the harness 'lives outside this repo' and names no path, repo or commit. It is 141 files in a session-scoped /private/tmp directory that will be garbage-collected, taking every number in 1148 lines of claims with it. The two commands given run but their counts are stale: auction-advisor prints 42, not 27; roster-manager 51, not 44. It lists 2 of 10 test files.
findings.fix: Move the harness into a tracked location or reference it by URL and commit SHA; list entry-point scripts per Part; replace hard-coded counts with a runner.

findings.title: Fabricated player news shipped as a live Game Day Assessment, never replaced
findings.evidence: Three hardcoded li claims including 'Christian McCaffrey (Questionable) is a game-time decision' and 'Kicker Harrison Butker has reduced projection' for a LAC vs DEN game — Butker is a Kansas City kicker. grep for matchup-weather-news in js/app.js returns nothing: unlike its siblings, this element is never written to, so the invented lines display permanently. Directly contradicts BACKTEST.md:8-9 and commit ee64f70.

findings.title: A concluding section contradicts Parts 5, 7 and 14 of the same document
findings.evidence: Says in-season management is 'not modelled at all' and roster-manager is 'currently unvalidated'. But Part 5 measures the waiver lever at +7.0pp over 300 seasons, Part 7 says lineups are now decided each week and tables five in-season levers, and Part 14 reports the full stack at 18.1%. It also anchors on 12.2% from Part 6, superseded by Part 14.

findings.title: Claims a rationale is 'recorded in the file' that does not exist
findings.evidence: Says the TD adjustment is 'deliberately absent from auction-advisor.js, with the reason recorded in the file'. Grep for td/touchdown/median/regression/snake/format across all 706 lines returns zero matches. draft-assistant.js mentions auction only in an unrelated docstring.
findings.fix: Add the snake-vs-auction asymmetry paragraph as a comment in auction-advisor.js, or drop the claim.

findings.title: The formula the docs call 'replaced' is still live in the UI
findings.evidence: BACKTEST.md Part 4 calls calculateAuctionBid 'catastrophically broken' and says replacing it is worth ~300 points a season. It is still exported with the exact condemned constants and called at app.js:1264 to populate the Target Bid column of the snake draft board.
findings.fix: State plainly that the replacement covers the auction board only, or route app.js:1264 through auction-advisor and delete the function.

findings.title: The most prominent number in the UI is unvalidated and nothing says so
findings.evidence: index.html:104 renders Championship Outlook at 3.5rem from preseasonOutlook and runSeasonSimulation. Grep for team-strength/preseasonOutlook/WEEKLY_SD in BACKTEST.md returns nothing — neither module is validated anywhere. simulator.js has no file header at all and 8% comment density; WEEKLY_SD = 22 drives the displayed probability with no stated source.

findings.title: '459 players' is stale; the set is now 523
findings.evidence: data/projections-2026.json has 523 players across 6 positions. Both locations still say 459. Git shows the drift is exactly one commit wide: e25550c wrote the 459 text, 9e3a767 thirteen minutes later grew the set and updated neither. player-database.js:10 WAS updated and says 523 — so the repo now states both numbers.

findings.title: The document says K and D/ST are excluded; the shipped app rosters and projects both
findings.evidence: Says 'K and D/ST are excluded throughout... roster construction here is 15 offensive spots'. The data now carries 33 kickers and 31 defenses; both auction-advisor and team-strength declare STARTER_SLOTS including D/ST and K; default roster is 9+7=16. findings.title: The only in-repo data-pipeline script cannot run

findings.title: A repo-root Test Runner Suite imports a module deleted long ago

findings.evidence: MISSING_INPUTS and NEWS_DERIVED_INPUTS both contain 'in-season trades', under a comment saying they are kept explicit so they cannot drift. news-monitor genuinely handles trades. app.js:2118 prints MISSING_INPUTS as 'Not yet wired to a data source, so not used', telling the user trade news is unused while the engine consumes it.

findings.title: No documentation of reloading, the version marker, or the debug helpers
findings.evidence: Covers first install and a happy-path sync and stops. Never mentions that Chrome caches content scripts and the extension must be reloaded after any edit — despite content-main.js:5-8 calling this 'the first thing to rule out'. Neither __GRIDIRON_EDGE_DEBUG__ nor __GRIDIRON_EDGE_REJECTED__ is documented. Two version strings exist with no stated relationship.
findings.fix: Add a Troubleshooting section: how to reload, what the version marker means, the debug helpers with sample output, and when to paste diagnose/syncheck/bidcheck.

findings.title: File headers are one-line labels on the modules that most need 'why'
findings.evidence: The repo convention is a substantial why-header. draft-assistant gets three lines despite being credited with the entire +47-point v5 rewrite; its body documentation is excellent, so this is purely a missing header. app.js is 2781 lines at 11% comments, espn-client 661 at 18%, store 384 at 16%. popup.js has no header at all at 6%.
findings.fix: Lift the existing inline rationale into a header for draft-assistant; add headers to app.js, store.js and popup.js.

findings.title: The board-depth comment no longer holds at 523 players
findings.evidence: PLAN_CANDIDATES = 110 with comments claiming the board contains the $1-3 tail. Computed against the current set for a 12x16 league: par at rank 110 is $3.73 and the $1 floor is not reached until about rank 150. The board truncates above the tail it claims to contain; the positional backfill mitigates this in practice, which is why no test catches it.
findings.fix: Derive board depth from leagueSize * rosterSize, or soften the comments to describe what 110 actually guarantees.

findings.title: Analyst-panel size differs between the backtest and the shipped data, unreconciled
findings.evidence: Describes inputs as 203-237 analysts and concludes 'a 200-analyst consensus is not beatable'. The shipped set is 88 experts, surfaced to users. Nothing reconciles whether the conclusion transfers. The generated field reads '8/07' with no year.

findings.evidence: Strong, consistently applied but undocumented conventions: ES modules with no build step; node --check is explicitly unsafe here and node test/syntax.test.mjs must be used instead; unknowns return null rather than a fabricated default; every parameter carries its fitting provenance; commit subjects are behavioural sentences.
findings.fix: Add a CLAUDE.md capturing the no-build-step rule, the node --check trap, the never-invent-a-number rule, comment-density expectations, and the requirement to update BACKTEST.md counts.

readability.justification: The codebase is two codebases wearing one coat. The newer engine modules are genuinely excellent — the why-comments explain real past bugs, and there is not a single commented-out block or TODO anywhere. But the older half has decayed badly, and the two halves are joined by duplicated logic that has provably diverged: three name normalizers that disagree on exactly the names a comment says once broke the app, two ESPN position tables that disagree about what a TE is, and two copies of the DOM scraper where each has the other's bug. Duplication that has already drifted is the most expensive readability failure there is.

findings.title: Third name normalizer disagrees with playerKey on exactly the names that once broke it
findings.evidence: normalizeName replaces apostrophes with a space; playerKey removes them, with a comment stating that spacing them produced 'ja marr chase' against a stored 'jamarr chase' and valued the consensus number one at replacement level. Ran both: Ja'Marr Chase gives 'ja marr chase' vs 'jamarr chase'; A.J. Brown 'a j brown' vs 'aj brown'. relevanceTo is called from app.js:2604 against roster names, so cross-module comparison cannot match apostrophe names at all.
findings.fix: Delete normalizeName and import playerKey. One normalizer, one file, one set of tests.

findings.title: Two ESPN position tables disagree; one maps tight ends to wide receiver
findings.evidence: content-main uses { 0:QB, 2:RB, 4:WR, 6:TE, 16:D/ST, 17:K } against p.player.defaultPositionId; espn-client maps the same field as { 1:QB, 2:RB, 3:WR, 4:TE, 5:K, 16:D/ST }. These are two different ESPN schemes — the content-script table is the lineupSlotId scheme, which espn-client itself documents. Applied to defaultPositionId, 4 means TE but the content script returns WR.
findings.fix: Extract one shared ESPN_IDS module with both maps explicitly named so the schemes cannot be confused.

findings.title: Two copies of the DOM scraper; each has the bug the other fixed
findings.evidence: popup.js carries the comment explaining the Round 1 snake-draft artefact and implements the fix; content-main.js:128 — the copy the manifest actually loads — still requires 'Round 1'. Conversely content-main uses a Map keyed by player identity while popup.js still has the Set-of-pick-numbers bug. Budget bounds diverged (260 vs 400). popup.js still attributes an unmatched drafter to teamId 1 where content-main deliberately uses null.

findings.title: playerDatabase read 77 lines before its const declaration (TDZ ReferenceError)

findings.title: getDraftRecommendations is a 315-line function
findings.evidence: Availability CDF, roster-need counting, snake arithmetic, TD regression, lineup value, survival model, risk weighting, tier warnings and prose generation in one body. Splits are already visible as banner comments at :118, :143, :241.

findings.title: recommendBid is 278 lines
findings.evidence: Builds par values twice and league state twice, backfills the board, binary-searches the ceiling, applies three separate caps, then builds four kinds of prose. The comment stack at :634-647 is three successive explanations of the same decision, appended rather than merged.

findings.title: checkAndSync is 236 lines and scrapeDraftDOM is 221
findings.evidence: checkAndSync does store extraction, DOM fallback, team reconciliation, drafter attribution with nested helpers defined inline, debug installation, progress parsing and change detection. scrapeDraftDOM declares NFL_NICKNAMES at a visibly different indentation level, a giveaway it was pasted in.

findings.title: renderHomePage is 278 lines with a mid-function return

findings.title: The playoff bracket is simulated from invented constants that ignore the teams
findings.evidence: randomNormal(115,10) vs (110,10), then (112,10) vs (112,10) — identical, so a coin flip — then (116,9) vs (114,9). None reads teamProjectionsPerWeek, so a 200-point roster and a 60-point roster have the same title odds once they reach the bracket. findings.evidence: projectedPoints > 13 for 'top TE', > 16 for 'top RB', and calculateAuctionBid's per-position baseline/multiplier table. auction-advisor states this function priced QBs at five times market. findings.title: MISSING_INPUTS lists inputs NEWS_DERIVED_INPUTS says are supplied

findings.title: week5Match holds the next unplayed fixture

findings.title: pct is a module-scope single-purpose formatter with a three-letter name
findings.evidence: Module scope in a 2781-line file, used only in two helpers. team-strength.js:244 has a different function also called pct.

findings.title: The 3-second sync poller swallows every failure with an under-describing comment

A render exception during a live draft is invisible and repeats every 3 seconds.

findings.evidence: Sweep of every export against all external references: describe, NEWS_DERIVED_INPUTS, pointsPerDollar, starterReserve, fetchTrending and TEAM_ALIASES have zero external references. playoffValue has zero references anywhere including its own file, despite a 12-line docstring claiming +1.1 points of championship probability.

findings.evidence: Zero references outside store.js across js/, test/ and index.html.
findings.fix: Delete deleteLeague; keep setPriorSeasonScoring only if the tdShare feed is imminent.

findings.title: Six timing constants, two named and four inline
findings.evidence: NEWS_TTL_MS and STALE_MS are named; the 8000ms fetch timeout, the 3000ms and 2000ms poll intervals and the 120-second staleness threshold are inline literals that interact — a reader must open three files to work out whether stale is reachable.

findings.evidence: Double-quoted console.log at :9 beside single-quoted console.warn at :707. Arrow functions throughout except the debug hook at :741, which uses function and var.
findings.fix: Normalise, or state in a header why the debug hook is deliberately ES5.

findings.title: Mixed async patterns across engines
findings.evidence: news-monitor uses async/await with a proper AbortController. espn-client.js:14-20 uses a bare module-level .then() with no .catch. app.js:1107 uses .then().catch(() => {}) — a swallowing catch — in an otherwise async-styled file.

findings.title: A 14MB scratch file and a space-containing script live in the served directory
findings.evidence: sleeper_players.json is 14,624,207 bytes, plus five other scratch files — all correctly gitignored but all sitting in the directory server.py serves. .gitignore lists both *.log and server.log redundantly.

Ran both normalizers in node against real names — the divergence is measured. Loaded mock-data.js: exactly 31 players. Loaded the projection file: 523 players, 88 experts. Reproduced the mapESPNLeague TDZ in node. Measured every function span with awk. Swept every export against external references. performance.justification: The algorithms are well-designed and the DOM layer is genuinely cheap (measured 4.7ms to build a 523-row table), but the render architecture is not built for a 3-second live loop. On the Live Draft tab in an auction the agent measured ~200ms of synchronous engine work per render, executed 3x per sync tick — 580-630ms of blocked main thread per 3s window — peaking early in the auction, exactly when the largest bids happen. Nothing is memoized anywhere, there is no Web Worker, no requestAnimationFrame, no debounce, and the extension's 2s loop performs its full-document scan before checking whether anything changed.

findings.title: targetBoard costs 213-334ms and runs on every Live Draft render
findings.evidence: Measured against the real 523-player DB, 12 teams: 274.4ms at 0 picks, 213.4ms at 12, 271.9ms at 24. Per call it fans out to 20 recommendBid, 234 planValue, 318,498 board-scan iterations and 269,479 lineupPoints calls. It is a watchlist that does not depend on currentBid at all, yet is recomputed whenever the bid ticks because the sync key includes nomBid.
findings.fix: Cache the watchlist keyed on (selections.length, drafted-id set, budgets) and skip recomputation when only currentNominationBid changed.

findings.title: Every sync renders the draft page three times
findings.evidence: checkLocalSyncFile -> importScrapedPayload -> saveLeague (notify #1 -> renderDraftPage) -> store.save() at espn-client.js:110 (notify #2 -> again) -> explicit renderDraftPage(mapped) at app.js:75. Measured one auction renderDraftPage at 209ms; x3 plus import = 628ms per 3s tick, 19-21% of wall clock, before any DOM cost. Two of the three renders are pure duplication.
findings.fix: Coalesce store notifications on a microtask, drop the redundant store.save() at espn-client.js:110, and delete the manual renderDraftPage — the subscriber already covers it.

findings.title: planValue rebuilds and re-sorts the whole lineup for all 110 candidates on every greedy iteration
findings.evidence: lineupPoints(have.concat([player])) inside a 110-item board scan inside a 16-slot while loop. Measured 1.19ms per planValue; recommendBid invokes it ~12x. A prototype keeping per-position sorted arrays and doing a trial splice insert ran in 0.405ms — 2.9x faster with a bit-identical result (1882.243825 both ways, same shopping list).
findings.fix: Maintain byPos sorted arrays across the greedy loop and compute marginal gain by trial insertion; only the best untaken candidate per position needs evaluating.

findings.title: All engine work runs on the main thread with no Worker and no yielding
findings.evidence: grep for Worker/requestAnimationFrame/requestIdleCallback/debounce/throttle across js/ and chrome-extension/ returns zero hits in the app. Every measurement above is a fully blocking main-thread stall. The only concession is a setTimeout(600) that defers but does not unblock.
findings.fix: Move recommendBid/targetBoard/preseasonOutlook into a Web Worker — they are pure functions over a serializable league object — and render from the message handler.

findings.title: recommendBid recomputes bid-invariant work on every keystroke
findings.evidence: bidInput.oninput -> draw(bid) -> full recommendBid. Measured 13.4-17.3ms per keystroke at full budgets (12 planValue, 15,587 board scans, 13,079 lineupPoints). currentBid is used only for action, winPrice and one trailing planValue; par values, board, planMissing, the binary search, starterReserve and subCap are all independent of it. The docstring claims it is safe on every keystroke — true at 192 picks (0.36ms), false at the start.
findings.fix: Split into priceContext(league, player) cached per league-state hash, plus a cheap atBid(context, currentBid) tail.

findings.title: The 2-second extension loop does its entire DOM scan before checking whether anything changed
findings.evidence: Per tick it unconditionally runs findCurrentNomination, findActiveRosterTeam, findMyTeamNameFromDOM (querySelectorAll('div') + innerText per div), findStoreState (querySelectorAll('*') + Object.keys per element), scrapeDraftDOM, and scrapeTeamsAndBudgets twice. The syncKey is computed and compared only after all of it. Measured in real headless Chrome on a 6,167-element page: cold scrapeTeamsAndBudgets 21.7ms; textContent control for the same loop 0.9ms, so innerText's layout dependency is ~24x the loop cost.
findings.fix: Compute a cheap change probe first and return early; call scrapeTeamsAndBudgets once; use textContent in filter passes and innerText only on survivors; cache the container and revalidate with isConnected.

findings.title: Object.values(db).find() inside a per-player, per-slot, per-week, per-team loop
findings.evidence: opponentDefense lookup reachable ~34,000 times, each scanning a 523-entry array — about 18M element visits. Measured runSeasonSimulation at 55ms with opponent absent and 445-454ms with opponent set, independent of runs. espn-client.js:581 sets opponent: 'OPP' for every API-imported player, so the scan always runs and always misses.
findings.fix: Build a dstByTeam Map once outside the loops; stop writing the placeholder 'OPP' sentinel.

findings.title: evaluateWaivers is O(n^2) over the free-agent pool
findings.evidence: positionalScarcity(freeAgents, p.position) filters and sorts the whole pool for each of ~500 candidates; blockingValue calls lineupGain for all 11 rivals, about 11,000 lineupBreakdown rebuilds per call. Measured 25.1ms at 523 FAs, 32.6ms at 475, 45.5ms at 331 — it gets slower as the pool shrinks because rosters fill. Runs on every renderWaiversPage and twice more on the home page.
findings.fix: Precompute scarcityByPosition once (6 entries) before the map; precompute each rival's baseline lineupBreakdown and compute gain incrementally.

findings.title: renderHomePage runs rankTeams four times and freeAgentsIn twice per render
findings.evidence: preseasonOutlook calls rankTeams internally, then rankTeams again at :768, then highestImpactMoves calls it at :817, then draftMovesHtml calls highestImpactMoves(league, freeAgentsIn(league)) again — a fourth rankTeams and a second full pool scan. rankTeams -> replacementLevels does Object.values(db) once per starting position, 6 full 523-entry scans per call, so 24 per render. Measured preseasonOutlook(1500) at 20.8ms (8 teams) / 30.6ms (12).
findings.fix: Compute ranked/moves/freeAgents once at the top of renderHomePage and thread them through; hoist Object.values(db) out of the position loop.

findings.title: A network fetch on every draft-page render
findings.evidence: checkDraftReadiness().then(...) is the first statement of renderDraftPage, issuing fetch('/health?cb=' + Date.now()). With three renders per 3s sync that is ~1 request/second, on top of the 26KB cache-busted imported_league.json every 3s. Neither fetch has an AbortController or timeout, and setInterval does not await, so a hung server lets requests accumulate.
findings.fix: Poll /health on its own 15-30s interval outside the render path; add AbortController with a ~2s timeout and an in-flight guard.

findings.title: Full-state JSON.stringify and setItem twice per sync, with silent quota failure
findings.evidence: Measured serialized state at 286KB for one 12-team league with the 523-player DB, 437KB with a second league. Called from saveLeague and again from store.save() at espn-client.js:110. Leagues are never pruned, so every leagueId ever synced persists a full DB copy — about 17 leagues reaches the 5MB quota. metricsHistory is capped at 40 per player, but that cap is itself 1,365KB for 523 players.
findings.fix: Store the shared playerDatabase once under its own key; debounce writes; surface quota failure; LRU-prune old leagues.

findings.title: findPlayer rebuilds and filters Object.values(db) on every lookup
findings.evidence: A full filter runs before any match attempt, then up to five more full passes. Measured 0.07ms per hit, 14.99ms for 200 lookups. espn-client.js:242 calls it once per pick inside importScrapedPayload, which re-runs on every 3s sync — 192 picks is ~15ms of pure re-derivation per tick, plus Object.assign copying 523 entries each time.
findings.fix: Build byKey/byPosition/bySurnameInitial index Maps once when the DB is created; make the import incremental.

findings.title: The championship page re-runs the Monte Carlo unconditionally on every render
findings.evidence: runIt() is called at the bottom of renderChampionshipPage, and renderPreseasonOutlook already ran at :2404 with runs = 3000; runIt then schedules 6000. One render = 9,000 simulated seasons. Measured 39.8ms + 82.9ms = ~120ms per render, on the same 3s notify loop.
findings.fix: Run the 6,000-run pass only from the button's onclick; memoize on a hash of (rosters, selections.length).

findings.title: The snake-draft table re-creates every row and does a document-wide getElementById per row
findings.evidence: Up to 523 rows appended one at a time with no DocumentFragment, plus a calculateAuctionBid per row. Measured in real headless Chrome: current 4.7ms, single innerHTML string 3.2ms, DocumentFragment 4.3ms, the 523 getElementById calls 0.2ms. Real but small — not a top-tier problem despite how the code looks.
findings.fix: Low priority: build one HTML string and use a delegated click listener on tbody.

findings.title: Three full Object.values(db) passes per recommendBid
findings.evidence: 1,569 element visits per call, x21 calls per render. Measured parValues(523) at 0.06ms, so ~2.5ms per render — real but dwarfed by planValue.
findings.fix: Hoist available/parById into a per-render context shared by targetBoard's 20 calls.

findings.title: The poll has no visibility gating
findings.evidence: setInterval(checkLocalSyncFile, 3000) with no document.hidden check. Chrome throttles background timers, which accidentally mitigates this — but the intended two-monitor setup keeps both foreground and pays full cost.
findings.fix: Skip when document.hidden and re-sync once on visibilitychange.

performance.verified: Read auction-advisor, team-strength, player-database and store in full, plus the relevant sections of app.js, roster-manager, simulator, lineup-optimizer, draft-assistant, news-monitor, espn-client and content-main. Wrote and ran four Node benchmarks against the real modules and real projection data at auction states of 0/12/24/48/96/192 picks — all millisecond figures are measured. Built an instrumented auction-advisor for exact call counts. Prototyped the incremental planValue and verified a bit-identical result at 2.9x speed. Measured DOM cost in real headless Chrome on a 6,167-element synthetic draft room and a 523-row table. Measured serialized localStorage size. Confirmed by grep: zero Workers, zero rAF, zero memoization, no listener leaks, bounded caches, correct AbortController on the news fetch.
performance.notChecked: Could not load the real ESPN draft room, so extension per-tick cost is measured against a synthetic page and is a lower bound. No Chrome DevTools traces of the live app — all app-side timings are V8-in-Node on an M-series Mac; a mid-range laptop will be 2-3x slower, so the ~600ms/3s figure is conservative. Did not measure real setItem wall time in Chrome. Did not exercise memory growth over a multi-hour draft. Did not profile popup.js or server.py under load.

security.justification: The server hardening is real and verified live on an isolated copy — loopback binding, path allowlist, per-origin CORS, body cap, shape check, atomic writes, no exception disclosure. The extension bridge and service worker now genuinely validate origin and sender. But XSS is not closed: an independent PoC produced three raw-markup injections in two panels plus a fourth proven at the string level, and the repo's own xss suite passes 12/12 while they are live because its fetch mock never exercises the news path. There is still no CSP, and the escaping refactor itself broke the live-draft panel by double-escaping generated markup.

findings.title: News headline injected unescaped into the waiver panel
findings.evidence: PoC recorded the sink write containing raw . app.js:2728 escapes the same field correctly — the inconsistency is the bug.
findings.fix: esc() the headline; use int() for the fallback count.

findings.title: Player name injected unescaped into the waiver news row
findings.evidence: ${x.player} with no esc, while the very next line escapes position and team.
findings.fix: esc(x.player).

findings.title: Article athlete tags joined into markup unescaped
findings.evidence: ${item.players.slice(0,3).join(' · ')} into news-list-container.innerHTML; two lines above, headline and why are escaped.
findings.fix: map(esc) before join.

findings.title: Simulator action plan injects player and manager names unescaped
findings.evidence: Drove the real runSeasonSimulation with a hostile roster: returned title containing raw markup. Reachable from the Championship page whenever a starter is Out.
findings.fix: esc() both, or return structured fields.

findings.title: Unescaped err.message in the news-failure panel
findings.evidence: V8's JSON parse error echoes the response body, so a hostile news response becomes markup. Proven end to end. Same pattern at app.js:955.
findings.fix: esc(err.message) at both sites.

findings.title: The escaping refactor broke the live-draft recommendation panel
findings.evidence: esc(stat(...)) double-escapes — stat() returns HTML. The Action tile renders its own div markup as visible text. Every sibling call is correctly unwrapped.
findings.fix: Unwrap it; escape style.label inside stat() instead.

findings.title: Draft rationale strings injected unescaped
findings.evidence: whyBest/advantage/riskLevel/planChange interpolate topPick.position from the scraped payload with no whitelist. Snake path only.
findings.fix: esc() all four; validate playerPosition against the known set.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy anywhere
findings.evidence: Confirmed absent from the markup and from every server response. Each sink above is therefore unmediated execution on the origin holding the league data.
findings.fix: Send a CSP header from end_headers(), plus nosniff.

findings.title: Any Chrome extension may read the league file and overwrite /sync
findings.evidence: origin.startswith('chrome-extension://') matches every extension id. A probe with a fabricated id got 200 and rewrote the temp copy's league file.
findings.fix: Pin the exact extension id; add a shared token.

findings.title: No Host header validation (DNS rebinding)
findings.evidence: curl -H 'Host: attacker.test' returned 200 with the full league body. Read-only, since POST still checks Origin.
findings.fix: Reject any Host not in the loopback set with 421.

findings.title: Popup host gate is a substring test
findings.evidence: tab.url.includes('fantasy.espn.com') is satisfied by https://evil.test/?ref=fantasy.espn.com; the popup then injects and POSTs whatever that page puts in __GRIDIRON_EDGE_LAST__.
findings.fix: Parse the URL and compare hostname exactly.

findings.title: allFrames:true re-opens the frame boundary the manifest closed
findings.evidence: The manifest sets all_frames:false, but both executeScript calls pass allFrames:true and take the first frame reporting success.
findings.fix: Drop allFrames, or filter to frameId 0.

findings.title: Quota failure is recorded but still never surfaced
findings.evidence: persistFailed and persistError are written and read nowhere; the docstring claims the failure 'is surfaced rather than swallowed'.
findings.fix: Read it in a banner; assert it in the store suite.

findings.title: The XSS suite passes while four sinks are live
findings.evidence: Its fetch mock throws for anything but projections, so the news paths never execute; it also stubs insertAdjacentHTML and setAttribute as no-ops.
findings.fix: Mock the news endpoints with hostile payloads; record every sink type.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is '*'
findings.evidence: Broadcasts the full scraped draft to any listener in the frame. The receiver does check origin, so not currently exploitable.
findings.fix: Target https://fantasy.espn.com explicitly.

findings.title: Sender check uses sender.url and skips shape validation
findings.evidence: sender.origin is the field Chrome guarantees; the worker also forwards without re-running looksLikeAScrape.
findings.fix: Check sender.origin and re-validate the payload.

findings.title: The duplicated scraper is only half collapsed
findings.evidence: findCurrentNomination, the store search and the 32-club map are still duplicated, and content-main's copy has bid parsing the popup's lacks.
findings.fix: Move the shared helpers into one file loaded by both.

findings.title: Attacker-controlled leagueId written to the server log unfiltered
findings.evidence: Newlines and ANSI escapes forge log lines in the operator's terminal.
findings.fix: repr() it or strip to a safe character class.

findings.title: localStorage restore validates only the top level
findings.evidence: leagues[x].teams may be any type; renderers index into it. This turns each sink above into a persistent rather than reflected injection.
findings.fix: Validate each restored league against the same predicate the server uses.

security.verified: Ran a copy of the server in a scratch directory on port 8931 and probed 30 paths across five traversal encodings, CORS for six origin classes, Host spoofing, POST origin enforcement, oversize and malformed bodies, and OPTIONS preflight. Wrote an independent XSS PoC instrumenting innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/setAttribute across all ten renderers with hostile news responses: 173 sink writes, 3 raw survivors, 44 correctly escaped. Drove the real runSeasonSimulation to prove the actionPlan strings carry markup. Confirmed no secrets across twelve git-history patterns and no dependencies.

Did not stand up a DNS-rebinding domain. Never POSTed to the live server or touched the real league file. The snake-draft branch was not reached dynamically.

tests.justification: Real progress — npm test exists, 13 suites and 350 assertions run green in 1.8s, and mutation testing confirms escape.js, store.js, player-database.js, the scraper's Set/Map crash and pick attribution are genuinely defended. But the bar is engine correctness: inflating every auction bid ceiling by 15% left all 350 assertions passing, while perf.test.mjs's header claims outputs are pinned and no pinned value exists. The documented coverage command fails reproducibly, this week's own dedup fix has no regression test, and a live XSS sink was proven that the xss suite structurally cannot see. Mutation kill rate 42%.

findings.evidence: The header claims pinned outputs. The only assertion is a string-format regex. Mutating maxBid to Math.round(lo*1.15) left the full suite passing while a mid-tier WR moved 29 -> 33.

findings.evidence: 3/3 runs: perf.test.mjs fails under instrumentation because the 12ms budget was written for uninstrumented runs. The command documented in the README is red.

findings.title: The duplicate-row dedup fix has no regression test

findings.evidence: No test imports it. Changing topPick to the WORST ranked player left the suite passing. High line coverage here is a false signal.

findings.title: simulator.js is entirely unexecuted
findings.evidence: 1.80% line, 0.00% function. Mutating the early return to fixed 50% values passed. Bare Math.random with no rng seam.

findings.title: lineup-optimizer and trade-generator can return nonsense silently
findings.evidence: Making an Out player score +100 — starting someone who cannot play — passed. So did making trade-generator return an empty array.
findings.fix: Direct suites: an Out player is never started; the flex is filled once; proposals improve the proposer.

findings.title: server.py has zero tests and is a trust boundary
findings.evidence: No Python test exists anywhere. The file's own header documents four security properties, none asserted.
findings.fix: Add a stdlib unittest suite covering the allowlist, CORS, body cap and malformed-body handling.

findings.title: popup.js is still a duplicated, diverged second scraper with zero tests
findings.evidence: The consolidation commit touched no extension file. Six helpers still duplicated, three verified diverged by byte length.
findings.fix: Extract the shared helpers; until then assert the two copies match.

findings.title: looksLikeAScrape, a security gate added this round, has no tests
findings.evidence: No test exercises it; extension files do not appear in the coverage report at all.
findings.fix: Extract and test against null, arrays, missing fields, circular and oversized payloads.

findings.title: A vacuous assertion in the store suite
findings.evidence: getActiveLeague() returns null anyway via `|| null`, so the check passes whether or not the clearing block exists. Deleting it passed.
findings.fix: Assert store.state.currentLeagueId === null directly.

findings.title: Four checks can still vanish silently
findings.evidence: Flipping the guard condition took the file from 42 passed to 38 passed, exit 0, with no signal.
findings.fix: Assert the fixture precondition, and add else-branches.

findings.title: process.exit(0) still masks late async failures in four files
findings.evidence: Injecting a late rejection before the exit call: the exit(0) form reported pass, the if(failed) form reported fail. Nine files converted, four not.
findings.fix: Use if (failed) process.exit(1) everywhere.

findings.title: The rng seam exists and is still unused
findings.evidence: preseasonOutlook takes rng; no test passes it. Assertions survive because they are loose inequalities, which is also why they kill no mutants.
findings.fix: Pass a seeded PRNG and pin exact outputs.

findings.title: elCache still leaks across scenarios
findings.evidence: written is cleared per scenario; elCache is not, so textContent, value and cssText persist.
findings.fix: elCache.clear() inside load().

findings.title: No CI
findings.evidence: No .github. The suite runs only when someone remembers, which is how the coverage command reached a reproducibly-red state unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the suite and coverage on push.

findings.title: renderNewsItems and the news fetch functions are unexecuted
findings.evidence: Every test's fetch rejects for non-projection URLs, so only the error branch runs. The rule the code implements — that 'no news' and 'feed down' are different facts — is asserted nowhere.
findings.fix: Stub a canned articles fixture and assert all three states.

findings.title: num() and int() have no direct tests
findings.evidence: 50% function coverage; these are the designated safe sink for untrusted numeric JSON.
findings.fix: Assert the fallback behaviour directly.

findings.title: The duplicate-pick case asserts only 'did not throw'
findings.evidence: Which pick survives, and whether both reach selections, is unasserted.
findings.fix: Assert both players land and selections.length === 2.

tests.verified: Ran npm test (13 files, 350 assertions, exit 0) and each file individually with per-file counts. Ran npm run coverage three times — fails identically each time. Applied 19 mutations to an isolated copy: 8 killed, 11 survived, kill rate 42%. Proved the app.js:2798 XSS end to end. Proved the silent assertion skip (42 -> 38, exit 0) and the process.exit(0) async mask side by side.

performance.justification: The highest-stakes claim is genuinely true and independently verified: 4,095 recommendBid comparisons across 81 league states against a from-scratch reference, all 14 fields, zero mismatches. Render coalescing is real — 1 render and 1 setItem per sync, measured — and targetBoard fell from 213-334ms to 63-153ms. But the hot path still blocks 42-94ms per tick on an M3 Pro with no Worker, no rAF, no debounce and no memoization anywhere; perf.test.mjs is demonstrably fake; and the new database index introduced a 256x cliff that is worse than the code it replaced.

findings.title: The equivalence guard tests nothing of the kind
findings.evidence: Mutating BENCH_WEIGHT from 0.12 to 0.20 — a constant that moves every bid ceiling — still printed 6 passed, 0 failed. CLAUDE.md and the README both cite this test as proof the answers did not change.
findings.fix: Pin real values in a checked-in fixture, or keep a reference planValue in the test and assert equality.

findings.title: 'the database is indexed, not rescanned' never calls findPlayer
findings.evidence: It measures plain property access on a literal key. Neutering buildIndex so findPlayer returns null for every name — the entire resolution layer dead — still passed.
findings.fix: Time findPlayer over the names and assert a resolution rate alongside the duration.

findings.title: The index staleness guard is a length comparison one keyless record defeats permanently
findings.evidence: buildIndex filters records without a string key, so the counts disagree forever and the index rebuilds on every lookup. Measured 190 lookups: 0.2ms clean, 51.2ms with ONE keyless record — 256x slower, and 3.4x worse than before the index existed. espn-client.js:559 and mock-data.js both produce keyless records.
findings.fix: Key every player at construction, and replace the length heuristic with an explicit version counter.

findings.title: Opponent-defense lookup is a full scan inside a quadruple-nested loop
findings.evidence: ~34,560 full 523-element scans. Isolated: runSeasonSimulation is 32.3ms without p.opponent and 396.2ms with it — the lookup alone is 364ms, 92% of the call. The ESPN import path sets opponent.
findings.fix: Build a dstByTeam Map once outside the loops.

findings.title: targetBoard still blocks 63-153ms per sync on the fastest consumer CPU
findings.evidence: Measured at 8 and 12 teams across 0-96 picks; targetBoard is 90-97% of all Live Draft engine work. Only 10-15% is hoistable. No Worker, rAF, debounce or memoization anywhere in the repo.
findings.fix: Move it into a Web Worker; memoize on drafted-ids plus budgets, since the shortlist does not change while a bid ticks.

findings.title: Every keystroke in the player search runs the full draft render
findings.evidence: Measured 79.8ms per keystroke at 24 picks, plus a /health round trip. The bid box is fine now at 3.3-4.6ms.
findings.fix: Debounce at ~150ms and split the table filter out of renderDraftPage.

findings.title: A /health fetch on every draft render, including every keystroke
findings.evidence: Unconditional at the top of renderDraftPage. Async so it does not block, but unthrottled.
findings.fix: Poll readiness on its own interval and read a cached value.

findings.title: The 2s extension loop scans before checking for change
findings.evidence: The syncKey comparison is the last thing checkAndSync does, after querySelectorAll('*'), two div sweeps with innerText reads, and body.innerText.
findings.fix: Compute a cheap change probe first; use textContent in the filter passes.

findings.title: scrapeTeamsAndBudgets is called twice per tick
findings.evidence: Identical results, nothing between them can change the DOM.
findings.fix: Call it once.

findings.title: The championship page runs 9,000 simulated seasons per render
findings.evidence: Measured 165.9ms, and the first 3,000 runs are overwritten by the second call milliseconds later.
findings.fix: Drop the first call; run the 6,000 only on button press and cache it.

findings.title: evaluateWaivers rescans the pool per free agent
findings.evidence: 28.3ms at 331 free agents, empirical scaling exponent 1.15. positionalScarcity filters and sorts the whole pool once per candidate.
findings.fix: Precompute scarcity per position; hoist the per-rival roster lookups.

findings.title: 135KB serialised to localStorage every 3 seconds
findings.evidence: Improved from two writes totalling 286KB to one of 138KB, but every league keeps its own full copy of the database and the whole thing is rewritten when only a bid changed.
findings.fix: Store the database once under its own key; debounce the write.

findings.title: The snake table rebuilds 523 rows with a getElementById each
findings.evidence: 523 separate layout invalidations plus a full-document lookup per row. Snake path only.
findings.fix: DocumentFragment plus one delegated listener.

findings.title: renderHomePage calls rankTeams four times
findings.evidence: Confirmed, but rankTeams is 0.1ms and freeAgentPool 0.4ms; the home page's 29.3ms is dominated by preseasonOutlook. Round 1 overstated this.
findings.fix: Thread one result through for clarity; the gain is under 1ms.

findings.title: findNominatedPlayer does two lowercasing scans per render
findings.evidence: Under 0.05ms — negligible. Noted only because findPlayer already answers this and is the repo's single resolver.
findings.fix: Use findPlayer.

performance.verified: Six independent benchmark scripts against the real modules and real 523-player data, warmed up, median of N. Built a from-scratch reference planValue from the docstring and diffed it over 4,095 recommendBid calls and 810 planValue calls: zero mismatches on all fields, shopping lists included. Instrumented localStorage and a counting listener on the real store to measure renders, writes and bytes per sync. Mutation-tested perf.test.mjs to establish empirically that it detects neither a changed bid ceiling nor a dead index.
performance.notChecked: Real browser measurement — all numbers are node on an M3 Pro, so DOM, layout and real setItem cost are excluded and the true per-tick block is higher, likely 3-5x on a typical laptop. The extension's runtime cost was read, not measured. No heap profiling. Whether the ESPN-API import path is in live use, which sets the practical severity of the index cliff.

performance.justification: All three previous fixes verified landed: 20 syncs produce exactly 20 deliveries and 10 identical ones collapse to 1; 0 of 20 clock-only mutation batches run the full scan while 20 of 20 bid ticks do; one import produces one store write. What remains is the largest single cost, untouched: targetBoard is bit-identical at bid $1 and $27 -- it never reads the bid -- yet is recomputed every tick, and is 82.4ms of an 85.8ms renderDraftPage. Over one 27-tick nomination that is 1,514ms blocked against 458ms keyed; over a 192-lot auction, 161s against 49s.
